Slots.maps_to: sts2_rl/monsters/base.py:Encounter.slots (default empty tuple) -- phrog_parasite.py's PHROG_PARASITE_ELITE = Encounter(id="phrog_parasite_elite", monster_classes=[PhrogParasite]) passes no slots= or monster_slots= kwarg
Slots.issue: PhrogParasiteElite.Slots = ["phrog", "wriggler1", "wriggler2", "wriggler3", "wriggler4"] (5 named rows). The sim's Encounter never declares slots/monster_slots for this unit, so `encounter.slots == ()` and every creature's `.slot_name` stays None -- both the initial PhrogParasite and, later, its 4 spawned Wrigglers (executed: `py audit/tools/encounter_probes_e2.py kin-phrog-slots` shows `encounter.slots=()` and `slot_name=None` on all 5 creatures after InfestedPower.on_death). This is filed under the shared mechanism encounter/_slot_row_unpopulated (also the_kin/Slots). DORMANT here specifically: the initial monster's slot has no reader I could find (grepped every C# `SlotName ==` site across src/ -- Exoskeleton, Myte, PhantasmalGardener, Wriggler; none check "phrog"); Wriggler's own move-key selection (which DOES branch on SlotName in C#) is separately and correctly reproduced via a `slot: int` constructor argument at the spawn site (InfestedPower.on_death in sts2_rl/powers.py passes slot=i+1, and Wriggler.__init__ uses `slot % 2` to pick NASTY_BITE vs WRIGGLE -- verified against C#'s wriggler1/3->NASTY_BITE, wriggler2/4->WRIGGLE pattern, byte-for-byte equivalent for the one-time initial-move check the C# state machine performs). So the observable first-move choice is right; only the introspectable slot_name string, the Encounter.slots row, and CombatState.sort_enemies_by_slot_name's ability to reorder this encounter's enemy list are unmodeled. The sim's Encounter dataclass CAN express a slot row (Fabricator/Ovicopter use it), so this is a per-unit omission, not a structural limitation.

HasScene.maps_to: none -- headless sim has no scene/rendering layer
HasScene.rationale: PhrogParasiteElite.HasScene => true (a bespoke combat layout scene). The sim never renders anything, so this and every other presentation member on this unit (ExtraAssetPaths) are bucketed the same way.

AllPossibleMonsters.maps_to: none -- the sim has no per-encounter monster-preview member
AllPossibleMonsters.rationale: Same zero-cost finding as overgrowth_crawlers/AllPossibleMonsters: full_env.py's global MONSTER_IDS vocabulary already covers Wriggler as a strict superset, and the C#'s other consumer (asset preload) has no sim counterpart at all.

ExtraAssetPaths.maps_to: none -- headless sim has no asset-path/overlay-rendering layer
ExtraAssetPaths.rationale: PhrogParasiteElite.ExtraAssetPaths preloads the Infection card's overlay sprite. InfectionCard itself is ported (sts2_rl/cards); only the visual overlay asset is out of scope for a headless sim.

GenerateMonsters.note: C# GenerateMonsters returns a single-element list [(PhrogParasite, "phrog")] -- note Wriggler is NOT part of the initial roster despite appearing in AllPossibleMonsters; it is summon-only (InfestedPower.AfterDeath). The sim's PHROG_PARASITE_ELITE likewise builds exactly one PhrogParasite and nothing else. Roster (1 monster, right class), order (trivial) and draw count (0) all match; the slot half of the tuple is verdicted separately under Slots above.
